---
title: "Does WMC support mind wandering (in the lab)?"
output:
  html_notebook: default
---
Exceprts from Pre-registration (https://aspredicted.org/kw8a5.pdf):

2) What's the main question being asked or hypothesis being tested in this study?
Can we replicate the Levinson, Smallwood, and Davidson’s (2012) Experiment 2 finding that higher-WMC subjects mind wandered (as measured by experimenter-controlled probes) more than lower-WMC subjects while completing a breath awareness task. Furthermore, we want to estimate the size of this effect with more precision than the original accomplished.

3) Describe the key dependent variable(s) specifying how they will be measured.
The key dependent variable in this study is the correlation between performance on working memory capacity (WMC) measurement tasks (i.e., complex span tasks) and the percentage of probes that subjects rate as 4 or higher (on a 6-point Likert scale). Scores of 4 or higher are considered task unrelated thoughts (TUTs). As in Levinson et al., we will measure WMC with the operation span task. In addition, we will measure WMC with a symmetry span task. The dependent variable in the complex span tasks will the number of memoranda recalled in the correct serial order. We will also form a WMC composite by converting these raw scores (one from each complex span task) into Z scores (means and standard deviations from the same sample) and averaging them.

5) Specify exactly which analyses you will conduct to examine the main question/hypothesis.
We will conduct correlation analyses between the individual complex span tasks and the percentage of TUTs (i.e., mind wandering) and a correlation between the WMC composite and percentage of TUTs. In the original work, Operation span task scores were square root transformed to adjust for skewness. We will conduct all analyses with span scores transformed and without transformation.

6) Any secondary analyses?
We will also analyze relations between complex span tasks (and the WMC composite) and percentage of TUTs in a 6 minute baseline task, a 20 minute breath counting task, and overall percentage of task unrelated thoughts across the three breathing tasks. In the awareness portion of the task we will examine the number of self-caught mind wandering reports. We will test if these relate to our complex span measures. We will look at self-caught mind wandering as raw counts and as a ratio with probe-caught mind wandering within the awareness task and the overall rate of mind wandering across the three breathing tasks.

8) Anything else you would like to pre-register? (e.g., data exclusions, variables collected for exploratory purposes, unusual analyses planned?)
We will follow Levinson et al. and convention by excluding complex span task scores where subjects do not make an 85% correct criterion in the processing portion of the task. Without looking at their data, we will also exclude subjects from analysis who experimenters judge to be noncompliant with task instructions (e.g., sleeping, obviously not following task instructions).

Levinson et al. used a community sample for this study who received payment for participation. In this replication, we will use university students who receive credit towards a course requirement

```{r load libraries, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(plotrix)
```

```{r read in operation span data}
# read in csv files from each semester
o <- read.table("BRospan.txt", header=TRUE, sep=",")
o1 <- read.table("opan add.txt", header=TRUE, sep=",")
```

```{r manipulate operation span data}
o <- filter(o, Procedure.Block. == "SessionProc")
o <- select(o, Subject, MathErrorTotal, OspanTotal)
#change variable names to id, er(processing errors), ospan (ospan score with partial credit scoring)
colnames(o) <- c("id","er","ospan")

o1 <- filter(o1, Procedure.Block. == "SessionProc")
o1 <- select(o1, Subject, MathErrorTotal, OspanTotal)
colnames(o1) <- c("id","er","ospan")

o <- rbind(o, o1)

os <- o %>%
 group_by(id)%>%
 filter(row_number()==1)

os$er <- as.numeric(as.character(os$er))
os$ospan <- as.numeric(as.character(os$ospan))
osp <- filter(os, er < 12)

#percentage of subjects who are excluded because of accuracy criterion
(nrow(os)-nrow(osp))/(nrow(os))
```

```{r read in symmetry span data}
# read in csv files
s <- read.table("BRsspan.txt", header=TRUE, sep=",")
s1 <- read.table("sspan add.txt", header=TRUE, sep=",")
```

```{r manipulate symmetry span data}
s <- filter(s, Procedure.Block. == "SessionProc")
s <- select(s, Subject, SymmErrorTotal, SspanTotal)
colnames(s) <- c("id","sser","sspan")

s1 <- filter(s1, Procedure.Block. == "SessionProc")
s1 <- select(s1, Subject, SymmErrorTotal, SspanTotal)
colnames(s1) <- c("id","sser","sspan")

s <- rbind(s, s1)

ss <- s %>%
 group_by(id)%>%
 filter(row_number()==1)

ss$sser <- as.numeric(as.character(ss$sser))
ss$sspan <- as.numeric(as.character(ss$sspan))
ssp <- filter(ss, sser < 7)

#percentage of subjects who are excluded because of accuracy criterion
(nrow(ss)-nrow(ssp))/(nrow(ss))
```

Below I break out the mind wandering data from the awareness (3rd) portion of the breathing task
After breaking it out and merging it, I aggregrate it to get a MW for every subjects
```{r break out awareness mind wandering}
b <- read.table("breathing.txt", header=TRUE, sep=",")
#colnames(b)
choices <- length(unique(b$Subject))
awa <- filter(b, Running.Block. == "AwarenessTask", Procedure.Trial. == "BreathTUT2", SubTrial == "1")
awa <- select(awa, "Subject","AwarenessTuT", "WhereATT4.RESP","AwareATT5.RESP")

b1 <- read.table("breath add.txt", header=TRUE, sep=",")
#colnames(b))
awa1 <- filter(b1, Running.Block. == "AwarenessTask", Procedure.Trial. == "BreathTUT2", SubTrial == "1")
awa1 <- select(awa1, "Subject","AwarenessTuT", "WhereATT4.RESP","AwareATT5.RESP")

awa <- rbind(awa, awa1)

awas <- awa %>%
mutate(mw =  ifelse(WhereATT4.RESP >3, 1, 0))%>%
 group_by(Subject)%>%
 summarise(mwa = mean(mw))
```

Below I break out the mind wandering data from the counting (2nd) portion of the breathing task
After breaking it out and merging it, I aggregrate it to get a MW rate for every subjects
```{r break out counting mind wandering}
cou <- filter(b, Running.Block. == "CountingTask", Procedure.Trial. == "BreathTUT1", SubTrial == "1")
#colnames(cou)
cou <- select(cou, "Subject","Trial", "WhereATT2.RESP","AwareATT3.RESP")

cou1 <- filter(b1, Running.Block. == "CountingTask", Procedure.Trial. == "BreathTUT1", SubTrial == "1")
cou1 <- select(cou1, "Subject","Trial", "WhereATT2.RESP","AwareATT3.RESP")

cou <- rbind(cou, cou1)

cous <- cou %>%
mutate(mw =  ifelse(WhereATT2.RESP >3, 1, 0))%>%
 group_by(Subject)%>%
 summarise(mwc = mean(mw))
```

Below I break out the mind wandering data from the baseline (1st) portion of the breathing task
After breaking it out and merging it, I aggregrate it to get a MW rate for every subjects
```{r break out breathing  mind wandering}
bre <- filter(b, Running.Block. == "BreathTUTList", Trial == "1")
#colnames(cou)
bre <- select(bre, "Subject", "WhereATT.RESP","AwareATT1.RESP")

bre1 <- filter(b1, Running.Block. == "BreathTUTList", Trial =="1")
#colnames(cou)
bre1 <- select(bre1, "Subject", "WhereATT.RESP","AwareATT1.RESP")

bre <- rbind(bre, bre1)


bres <- bre %>%
mutate(mw =  ifelse(WhereATT.RESP >3, 1, 0))%>%
 group_by(Subject)%>%
 summarise(mwb = mean(mw))
```


Below I add up probe data across sections to compute a sum of MW probes indicating MW
```{r combining mw data aross sections and getting a sum of probes indicating MW}
awm <- select(awa, "Subject", "WhereATT4.RESP")
colnames(awm) <- c("id","mw")
brem <- select(bre, "Subject", "WhereATT.RESP")
colnames(brem) <- c("id","mw")
coum <- select(cou, "Subject", "WhereATT2.RESP")
colnames(coum) <- c("id","mw")
cumw <- bind_rows(awm, brem, coum)
cumw_sum <- cumw %>%
mutate(mw1 =  ifelse(mw >3, 1, 0))%>%
 group_by(id)%>%
 summarise(mw_sum = sum(mw1))
colnames(cumw_sum)[1] <- "Subject"
```


Below I add up probe data across sections to figure out a cumulative MW rate (proportion of thought probes with responses greater than 3)
```{r combining mw data aross sections and getting a cumulative MW rate}
awm <- select(awa, "Subject", "WhereATT4.RESP")
colnames(awm) <- c("id","mw")
brem <- select(bre, "Subject", "WhereATT.RESP")
colnames(brem) <- c("id","mw")
coum <- select(cou, "Subject", "WhereATT2.RESP")
colnames(coum) <- c("id","mw")
cumw <- bind_rows(awm, brem, coum)
cumw1 <- cumw %>%
mutate(mw1 =  ifelse(mw >3, 1, 0))%>%
 group_by(id)%>%
 summarise(mwcu = mean(mw1))
colnames(cumw1)[1] <- "Subject"
```

Below I extract data for self caught probes and sum up the # of self caught probes by subject
```{r self caught probes}
awasc <- filter(b, Running.Block. == "AwarenessTask")
awasc <- select(awasc, "Subject","Wait4TUTSlide2.RESP")
#
#b1 <- read.table("breath add.txt", header=TRUE, sep=",")
awasca <- filter(b1, Running.Block. == "AwarenessTask")
awasca <- select(awasca, "Subject","Wait4TUTSlide2.RESP")

awasc <- rbind(awasca, awasc)

awasc1 <- awasc %>%
mutate(sc =  ifelse(Wait4TUTSlide2.RESP == "{CONTROL}", 1, 0))%>%
 group_by(Subject)%>%
 summarise(sct = sum(sc))
```

Merge MW rates from three sections (and cumulative) with complex span scores
Create new variables for span scores (square them to match Levinson et al.). Make a WMC composite
```{r make a complete data set}
fu <- left_join(awas,awasc1, by ='Subject') %>%
                left_join(., bres, by='Subject')%>%
                        left_join(., cous, by = 'Subject')%>%
                                left_join(., cumw_sum, by = 'Subject')%>%
                                        left_join(., cumw1, by = 'Subject')
#head(fu)
colnames(fu)[1] <- "id"
ful <- left_join(fu,osp, by ='id') %>%
                left_join(., ssp, by='id')
ful <- select(ful,id, mwa, mwb, mwc, mwcu, sct,mw_sum, ospan, sspan)

#make new variables
ful$osq <- ful$ospan^2
ful$ssq <- ful$sspan^2
ful$sz <- scale(ful$sspan)
ful$oz <- scale(ful$ospan)
ful$ssqz <- scale(ful$ssq)
ful$osqz <- scale(ful$osq)
ful$wmcz <- (ful$sz + ful$oz)/2
ful$wmcsqz <- (ful$ssqz + ful$osqz)/2

ful$scrat <- (ful$sct/ful$mw_sum)

ful$scrat[is.nan(ful$scrat)] <- NA
ful$scrat[is.infinite(ful$scrat)] <- NA
ful$scrat<- as.numeric(as.character(ful$scrat))

ful$scrat_sr <- sqrt(ful$scrat)
write.csv(ful,"LSDRep_fullagg.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```
##Descriptive statistics including subjects who will later be removed;notice 220 subject with 2 good span scores
mwa = Awareness Mind Wandering; mwb = Baseline Mind Wandering; mwc = Counting Mind Wandering; mwcu = Cumulative Mind Wandering;
sct = Count of self-caught; mw_sum = sum of probe-caught mw; ospan = operation span partial score; sspan = symmetry span partial score;
osq = squared operation span; ssq = squared symmetry span; sz = Z score of sym span; oz = Z score of operation span; ssqz = Z score of squared symmetry span;
osqz = Z score of squared operation span; wmcZ = working mmeory composite; wmcsqz = WMC composite using squared scores; scrat = ratio of self caught to probe caught MW; scrat_sr = square root of ratio of self caught to probe caught MW

```{r descriptives for complete data}
max <- round(apply(ful[,c(2:19)],2,max, na.rm = TRUE),2)

skew <- round(apply(ful[,c(2:19)],2,skew, na.rm = TRUE),2)
kurtosis <- round(apply(ful[,c(2:19)],2,kurtosi, na.rm = TRUE),2)

#write.csv(descr,"breathing task desc all.csv")

```

#Correlations with inferentials
##Frequentist pearson correlation of Awareness Mind-wandering and squared operation span
```{r replication of Levinson et al. Exp 2 osp and Mw correlation}
cor.test(ful$mwa, ful$osq)
```
##Bayesian Credibility interval for Awareness Mind-wandering and squared operation span
```{r to produce Bayesian credible interval}
bayes.cor.test(ful$mwa, ful$osq)
```
##BF for Awareness Mind-wandering and squared operation span
```{r replication of Levinson et al. Exp 2 osp and Mw correlation Bayesian inference testing against null}
rosqmwa <- cor(ful$mwa, ful$osq, use = "pairwise.complete.obs")
nosqmwa <- countNonNAEntries(ful$mwa, ful$osq)
bfosqmwa <- bf10JeffreysIntegrate(n=nosqmwa, r=rosqmwa)
bfosqmwa 
```
BF favors alternate over null but not strongly


##Code below provided by Alexander Ly##
##One-sided replicaiton Bayes Factor
```{r Rep Bayes Factor}
source("common.R")
source("correlationbayesian.R")

# Fill in the original and replication result
nOri <- 42
rOri <- 0.33

nRep <- 253
rRep <- -0.1622

bfObject <- .bfCorrieRepJosine(nOri=nOri, rOri=rOri, nRep=nRep, rRep=rRep)


rhoDomain <- seq(-1, 1, by=0.01)
zeroIndex <- which(rhoDomain==0)


# Here an example with a one-sided (plus-sided) replication attempt
# For the full posterior change 
#   .priorRhoPlus      to  .priorRho
#   .posteriorRhoPlus  to  .posteriorRho
# 
myFirstPriorLine <- .priorRhoPlus(rho=rhoDomain)
myPosteriorGivenDOriLine <- .posteriorRhoPlus(n=nOri, r=rOri, rho=rhoDomain)
mySecondPriorLine <- myPosteriorGivenDOriLine

# Plus sided posterior
myPosteriorGivenAll <- .stretchedBeta(rhoDomain, bfObject$combined$betaA, bfObject$combined$betaB)/(1-pbeta(1/2, bfObject$combined$betaA, bfObject$combined$betaB))
myPosteriorGivenAll[rhoDomain < 0] <- 0

# Two-sided posterior
# myPosteriorGivenAll <- .stretchedBeta(rhoDomain, bfObject$combined$betaA, bfObject$combined$betaB)

maxY <- 1.05*max(myFirstPriorLine, myPosteriorGivenDOriLine, myPosteriorGivenAll)


par(cex.main=3, mgp=c(3.5, 1, 0), cex.lab=2.5, font.lab=2, cex.axis=1.3, 
    mar=c(5, 6, 4, 7)+0.1, bty="n", las=1)
plot(0, 0, xlab=expression(rho), axes=FALSE, ylab="", ylim=c(0, maxY), col="white")
axis(1)
axis(2)
lines(rhoDomain, myFirstPriorLine, lwd=3, lty=3, col="grey")
lines(rhoDomain, mySecondPriorLine, lwd=3, lty=2, col="dimgrey")
lines(rhoDomain, myPosteriorGivenAll, lwd=3)

points(0, mySecondPriorLine[zeroIndex], pch=21, cex=2.5, bg="grey")
points(0, mySecondPriorLine[zeroIndex], cex=2.5, lwd=3)

points(0, myPosteriorGivenAll[zeroIndex], pch=21, cex=2.5, bg="grey")
points(0, myPosteriorGivenAll[zeroIndex], cex=2.5, lwd=3)


legend("topright", c(expression(paste(pi["-"], "(",rho, ")")),
                     expression(paste(pi["-"], "(",rho, "|d"['ori'], ")")),
                     expression(paste(pi["-"], "(",rho, "|d"['comb'], ")"))),
       lwd=c(2, 2, 2), lty=c(3, 2, 1), col=c("grey", "dimgrey", "black"),bty='n', cex=1.3)



bfObject$repGivenOri$bfPlus0
1/(bfObject$repGivenOri$bfPlus0)
```

##Confirmatory Factor Analysis with latent working memory and mind wandering variables
```{r CFA}
MY.model <- ' WMC =~ ssqz + osqz
              MW =~ mwa + mwb + mwc'

fit <- cfa(MY.model, data=ful, 
           std.lv=TRUE,  
           missing="fiml")

fitMeasures(fit)[c('chisq', 'df', 'pvalue', 'cfi', 'rmsea', 'srmr')]
summary(fit)
parameterEstimates(fit, standardized=TRUE)
```

In the awareness portion of the task I examined the number of self-caught mind wandering reports. I tested if these relate to complex span measures. I looked at self-caught mind wandering as raw counts and as a ratio with probe-caught mind wandering within the awareness task and the overall rate of mind wandering across the three breathing tasks.

##Code below provided by Alexander Ly##
##One-sided replicaiton Bayes Factor
```{r Rep with nontransformed operation span Bayes Factor}
source("common.R")
source("correlationbayesian.R")

# Fill in the original and replication result
nOri <- 42
rOri <- 0.33

nRep <- 253
rRep <- -0.1510

bfObject <- .bfCorrieRepJosine(nOri=nOri, rOri=rOri, nRep=nRep, rRep=rRep)


rhoDomain <- seq(-1, 1, by=0.01)
zeroIndex <- which(rhoDomain==0)


# Here an example with a one-sided (plus-sided) replication attempt
# For the full posterior change 
#   .priorRhoPlus      to  .priorRho
#   .posteriorRhoPlus  to  .posteriorRho
# 
myFirstPriorLine <- .priorRhoPlus(rho=rhoDomain)
myPosteriorGivenDOriLine <- .posteriorRhoPlus(n=nOri, r=rOri, rho=rhoDomain)
mySecondPriorLine <- myPosteriorGivenDOriLine

# Plus sided posterior
myPosteriorGivenAll <- .stretchedBeta(rhoDomain, bfObject$combined$betaA, bfObject$combined$betaB)/(1-pbeta(1/2, bfObject$combined$betaA, bfObject$combined$betaB))
myPosteriorGivenAll[rhoDomain < 0] <- 0

# Two-sided posterior
# myPosteriorGivenAll <- .stretchedBeta(rhoDomain, bfObject$combined$betaA, bfObject$combined$betaB)

maxY <- 1.05*max(myFirstPriorLine, myPosteriorGivenDOriLine, myPosteriorGivenAll)


par(cex.main=3, mgp=c(3.5, 1, 0), cex.lab=2.5, font.lab=2, cex.axis=1.3, 
    mar=c(5, 6, 4, 7)+0.1, bty="n", las=1)
plot(0, 0, xlab=expression(rho), axes=FALSE, ylab="", ylim=c(0, maxY), col="white")
axis(1)
axis(2)
lines(rhoDomain, myFirstPriorLine, lwd=3, lty=3, col="grey")
lines(rhoDomain, mySecondPriorLine, lwd=3, lty=2, col="dimgrey")
lines(rhoDomain, myPosteriorGivenAll, lwd=3)

points(0, mySecondPriorLine[zeroIndex], pch=21, cex=2.5, bg="grey")
points(0, mySecondPriorLine[zeroIndex], cex=2.5, lwd=3)

points(0, myPosteriorGivenAll[zeroIndex], pch=21, cex=2.5, bg="grey")
points(0, myPosteriorGivenAll[zeroIndex], cex=2.5, lwd=3)


legend("topright", c(expression(paste(pi["-"], "(",rho, ")")),
                     expression(paste(pi["-"], "(",rho, "|d"['ori'], ")")),
                     expression(paste(pi["-"], "(",rho, "|d"['comb'], ")"))),
       lwd=c(2, 2, 2), lty=c(3, 2, 1), col=c("grey", "dimgrey", "black"),bty='n', cex=1.3)



bfObject$repGivenOri$bfPlus0
1/(bfObject$repGivenOri$bfPlus0)
```
